To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the classification accuracy of the models depends on the signal features used as input data, 2) the accuracy of the models is influenced by the presence of noise, and 3) the accuracy of models depends on the number of samples in the dataset.
the classification accuracy is higher in the case of the dataset which contains the statistical features of the signals (i.e., the features extracted from the time domain and the frequency domain).
the performance of the deep learning models is significantly affected by the presence of noise and the type of the dataset used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of different deep learning models in a classification problem where we have a large number of features (input variables) and a small number of samples (training data) available.
the following questions: (i) what is the effect of the type of signal features (e.g. spectrogram) on the performance of a classifier model?
the performance of different neural network architectures for modulation classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the MC algorithm depends on the type of the signal and the type of the noise present in the signal.
the classification performance of deep learning models is highly dependent on the type of input signal features, while the choice of classifier model plays a secondary role.

, for a deep learning MC algorithm, it is not enough to only have a large and diverse enough training set, as the type of the signal impairments in the data also affects the classification accuracy and the model performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the deep learning models are capable of learning the signal features from the raw data without the need for feature extraction, and that the classification accuracy is highly dependent on the type of dataset used for training.
the performance of the MC systems is highly dependent on the signal features, and the presence of noise.

the classification performance can be significantly improved when the input data includes signal features which are not directly observable by the user (such as the spectral features), and when a deep learning model is used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the classifier and the type of the data are equally important factors for achieving high performance in MC.
the performance of the deep learning MC algorithms is significantly affected by the type of dataset used, which can be explained by the fact that the deep learning algorithms are data-driven.
, for the considered deep learning models, the classification performance is highly dependent on the type of the signal impairments.
